podcast.body: Recorded during 1993–94, this album was named after a live music venue in Vancouver. Singles included "Ocean Pearl," "Radio Love Song," and others. The album appeared alongside a wave of other Canadian rock records during the height of the Can Rock Renaissance, alongside Matt Good, Tea Party, I Mother Earth, Barenaked Ladies, Sloan, Tragically Hip, Blue Rodeo, Odds, Grapes of Wrath, Cowboy Junkies, Alanis Morissette, Treble Charger, The Watchmen, Crash Test Dummies, and many others. The band was notably never on any edition of Big Shiny Tunes. "The 90s is when the Canadian rock scene was healthy, wealthy and wise."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was the band's sixth record, released around 1995. Its release preceded a period of transition where the band was dropped by Warner and subsequently picked up by Sony Music Canada. "We ended part one in about 1995 with the band releasing their sixth record, Smiling Buddha Cabaret."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
